title: Temperature Alert
story: You're building a smart thermostat dashboard. Temperatures range from freezing to scorching. At -5°C, you want a blue "Freezing!" alert. At 22°C, a green "Normal." At 42°C, a red "Extreme heat!" Each alert carries the actual temperature so the UI can show the number.
why: An enum with data in each variant models sensor alerts where the severity determines the message but data flows with the variant.
analogy: Alert is like a weather siren. The temperature is the sensor reading. Check_temperature is the person watching the dial: "Under 0? Sound the cold siren. Over 40? Sound the extreme siren." The message method is the recorded voice that plays through the speakers.
try_it: Add a `Freezing(temp: Int)` variant for temperatures below -10°C. Test temperatures from -15 to 50 in steps of 5. Add a `Alert.color(self) -> Str` method returning CSS colors: Normal=green, Hot=orange, Cold=blue, Extreme=red.
tips: Check the most extreme cases first (>= 40, <= 0) so the order of `if` statements creates a priority system
Normal carries no data — when everything is fine, there's nothing extra to report
The `temp` field flows from `check_temperature` into the Alert variant, then out again in `message`
common_mistakes: Checking `celsius > 0` before `celsius <= 0` — a value of -5 passes > 0? No, but the order still matters for readability
Creating a Hot alert for 22°C — the threshold is 30, so 22 should be Normal
